key_insight: APOE associations with dementia, liver disease and plasma proteins varied by ancestry, while SNAP25 increased with ε4 dosage across ancestries.
clinical_relevance: These findings support ancestry-aware research into APOE-related risk and biomarkers, but do not establish clinical tests or treatment strategies.
method: Tested APOE genotype associations with 2,632 phenotypes across six genetic ancestry groups.
Adjusted for demographic and genetic covariates and assessed sex- and ancestry-related heterogeneity.
Evaluated APOE ε2 and ε4 dosage associations with plasma proteins across five ancestries.
evidence_signal: The study included 367,757 participants in phenome-wide analyses and 9,132 in proteomic analyses, identifying 27 associated phenotypes and nine associations with ancestry-specific effects.
watch_item: This observational APOE study is not AI cancer drug discovery research; its associations and candidate biomarkers require independent validation.
paper_title: Phenome-wide and proteomic analysis of APOE alleles across different ancestries in the All of Us Research Program
